# Customer-outcome copy — evidence audit and reusable template

Date: 2026-10-22. Status: internal editorial proposal for DTRT Co-Founder review. Source brief: Ian asked to break down, research, audit and implement the shared Brian Tracy reel. Recovery guidance DTRT-OPS-2026-10-22.1 acknowledged. This document proposes a content workflow; it does not establish adoption by other agents, a verified product, or permission to publish.

## Decision

Lead product messages with a specific customer situation and an achievable, verified benefit. Immediately show the mechanism or real use, then provide relevant specifications and purchase terms. Keep the public business experiment transparent, with its background below the customer proposition. Outcome language is a hypothesis to test, not evidence that the item delivers the outcome.

Retain the existing brand floor and social template in `social-lab-caption.md`. Current positioning, prices, public offers, publication approvals and commerce gates remain governed by AGENTS.md and Co-Founder. This template never selects a product or invents a feature. Proposed copy remains unpublished until its exact SKU evidence and owner approval exist.

## Video audit

Source: https://www.facebook.com/reel/3744824028984363 (canonical reel, accessed 2026-10-22); shared link: https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1L8fEQKtPT/?mibextid=wwXIfr.
Observed public page: Brian Tracy verified account; caption advocates selling customer results rather than features; event imagery matches Nordic Business Forum. The video was publicly playable after dismissing the login overlay. No downloadable media/transcript was exposed, so this is a thematic audit corroborated against original speaker materials and the event source, not a certified word-for-word transcript or timestamp audit. Facebook's automatic AI summary is not treated as research evidence.

|Theme or claim|Audit conclusion|Editorial application|
|---|---|---|
|People evaluate what a purchase changes for them|Useful customer-value heuristic; not an exclusive account of every purchase|Name the user's task or problem before the product's specification list|
|Most motivation is future anticipation, presented as 85% future / 15% past|Repeated in Tracy's own workbook, but no empirical study supporting this universal split was identified in inspected materials or targeted research|Do not repeat the ratios as scientific facts or use them in projections|
|Spend 90% on the destination and 10% on the vehicle|Presentation metaphor, not a validated allocation rule|Use outcome plus concrete demonstration and relevant details; don't enforce a numerical copy ratio|
|Customers buy improvement|Too broad if treated as a universal law: replacement, familiarity, aesthetics, habit, gifts and identity can matter|Treat the intended benefit as a testable reason to choose this exact item|
|Customers do not care about the company|Overstatement; seller credibility and delivery/return terms can affect a new store's purchase risk|Put buyer relevance first, then explain the seller and the test honestly|

## Research and limits

All links checked 2026-10-22. These foundational studies and original event materials are older than twelve months; they do not establish a current platform benchmark or forecast for this pilot. No cross-study percentages or expected sales lift are inferred.

|Primary source|What it supports|What it does not establish|
|---|---|---|
|[Brian Tracy workbook, What People Really Want](https://s3.amazonaws.com/bgs.briantracy.com/Workbooks/PGS%20-%20What%20People%20Really%20Want.pdf)|Confirms the speaker's stated motivation framework and ratios|Not independent experimental evidence for those ratios; publication date not established from the document|
|[Nordic Business Forum: Brian Tracy on Sales, 2012](https://www.nbforum.com/newsroom/videos/brian-tracy-on-sales-nordic-business-forum-2012/)|Original event context for the sales advice|An empirical marketing trial|
|[Escalas and Luce, 2004, Journal of Consumer Research](https://academic.oup.com/jcr/article-abstract/31/2/274/1824946), DOI10.1086/422107|Process versus outcome emphasis interacts with involvement and argument strength|Outcome-only messaging is always superior. The inspected abstract reports context-dependent differences; full study details not fully inspected|
|[Packard and Berger, 2021, Journal of Consumer Research](https://academic.oup.com/jcr/article/47/5/787/5873524?login=false), DOI10.1093/jcr/ucaa038|Concrete language in service encounters can improve perceived listening and customer responses|A measured conversion lift for a new dropshipping product page; applying it here is an inference|
|[Thompson, Hamilton and Rust, 2005, Journal of Marketing Research](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1509/jmkr.2005.42.4.431)|Consumers can overweight capabilities before use and usability after use|Features never matter, or that hiding specifications increases satisfaction. Abstract inspected; paywalled full text not claimed read|
|[FTC advertising substantiation policy](https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/ftc-policy-statement-regarding-advertising-substantiation)|Objective advertising claims need an appropriate evidentiary basis|A benefit-focused headline is exempt from substantiation|

## Audit of the current DTRT drafts

1. **Founder-first umbrella:** the previous umbrella opens with whether AI can earn its keep and the pilot's goals. Those are meaningful transparency context, but do not explain a customer's use for the item. Put a customer task, visible action and honest product detail first in product posts. Retain experiment context separately; do not erase it.
2. **Category-level vagueness:** previous hooks such as "Something useful for your space" are safe but indistinct. Replace them with the exact task and a supported outcome after SKU verification. If we cannot name a meaningful use, do not fill the gap with transformation claims.
3. **Features need a bridge:** retain dimensions, capacity, materials, settings, battery and compatibility. Explain how a verified feature supports a practical use rather than listing specifications alone or hiding them.
4. **Evidence risk in PR83:** inspected head `cea03fa59fcfcb3c89bc1cc443e5e990b3ca050f` keeps orders closed, but contains concrete US shipping windows while also saying they are not reconfirmed. The implementation owner should replace unsupported timing with a plain unverified/preview status until evidence exists. A disclaimer does not substantiate a positive shipping claim. Recheck current head before editing; this observation can become stale.
5. **Retired concepts:** earlier bottles, lamps and sliders were not verified available. Do not generate a finished sales claim or functional demo for a different replacement SKU merely because it shares a category.
6. **Proof is narrower than illustration:** generated animation must not stand in for evidence that the actual item moves, adheres, cleans, supports weight or keeps time as shown. Prefer licensed exact-SKU footage or truthful static imagery; identify illustrations.

## Copy workflow: situation, benefit, mechanism, evidence, terms

Planning fields (internal, never publish brackets):

```text
SKU / supplier / variant:
Customer and specific situation:
Main practical benefit:
Verified mechanism that enables it:
Evidence URL or account record, observed date, exact scope:
Limits / compatibility / care / safety:
Actual price and availability:
Confirmed shipping, returns and contact:
Owner-approved destination and CTA:
```

If a field lacks evidence, label it UNVERIFIED internally and keep customer copy in preview. No health, therapy, anxiety, sleep, weight-loss, guaranteed focus, quantified time savings or sales promises without the necessary evidence and authority. Ordinary purpose wording is still subject to the actual product working as described.

Page order:

1. Specific task/use headline, plus exact product identity.
2. Licensed exact-SKU image/demonstration; label any illustration.
3. One factual sentence connecting mechanism to use.
4. Price, actual availability, variant, dimensions and relevant limits.
5. Shipping/returns/contact before purchase commitment.
6. Brief founder-test disclosure and results link, if approved.

Internal template:

```text
Headline: [SPECIFIC CUSTOMER USE]
Description: [PRODUCT] uses [VERIFIED FEATURE] to [SUPPORTED PRACTICAL FUNCTION].
Fit: Designed for [VERIFIED USE/COMPATIBILITY]. Check [RELEVANT LIMIT].
Details: [SIZE / MATERIAL / SETTINGS / POWER / CARE AS APPLICABLE].
Terms: [ACTUAL PRICE / AVAILABILITY / VERIFIED SHIPPING / RETURN POLICY].
Disclosure: Part of DTRTLab's public product test.
CTA while held: View the preview. Orders are not open.
CTA only after commerce approval: See product details and delivery options.
```

## Conditional replacements for the previous category hooks

These are ready-to-adapt drafts, not verified product claims. Use each only after the stated feature has been verified for the selected SKU. They do not name a currently approved item or propose a price.

|Category|Headline/hook draft|Mechanism-to-use sentence draft|Verification required|
|---|---|---|---|
|Fitness/routine|Keep your mat and essentials together.|Carry your yoga mat and smaller items in one bag, using its mat compartment and pockets.|Exact compartment fit, closures, dimensions and carrying design; no exercise/health outcome implied|
|Home|Pick up pet hair from upholstery.|Roll across a compatible fabric surface to collect loose pet hair.|Actual collection mechanism, suitable fabrics, refill/cleaning requirements; no unsupported one-pass or damage-free guarantee|
|Adult desk toy|A small motion for your desk.|Give the spinner a turn and watch the pattern move.|Actual movement, noise, required parts and safety; no anxiety or focus outcome|
|Tactile|Fold, turn, repeat.|Move the connected sections through their folding sequence.|Actual hinge design, intended audience and safety; no calm/therapy claims|
|Productivity/desk|Give your laptop a raised place.|Set the stand to a supported position and check the fit for your device.|Load, device size, adjustment positions, stability; no posture/neck-pain promise|

If the approved productivity item is instead a timer: use "Give this task a clear endpoint" only when its countdown and completion signal are verified; show the actual setup steps and power requirements. Never imply a timer treats ADHD or guarantees deep work.

Founder-test disclosure draft: "I'm testing a small DTRTLab collection and sharing what actually sells and what it costs. Check the product details and delivery terms before deciding."

Preview umbrella draft: "A place for everyday tasks: carrying your gear, clearing a surface, or setting up your desk. I'm reviewing a small DTRTLab collection and sharing the process. Product previews are available; orders are not open."

These drafts preserve the real status at preparation time. The active owner must recheck whether previews and order states are actually available before use.

## Video template — editorial recommendation, not research-derived timing

For one short clip, sequence: a recognizable task/problem; the exact product in real use; the visible result; relevant product identity/limits; then approved CTA and experiment disclosure. Keep the first visual understandable without audio. A specific duration or three-second hook is a creative convention, not a proven conversion law.

Avoid opening every product clip with AI tools, revenue targets, model names or our production process. Those fit an optional behind-the-scenes post, clearly separated from the product proposition. Do not claim customer results from illustrative visuals.

## Low-budget verification plan

Hypothesis: for a qualified SKU, specific use + credible demonstration yields more qualified interest than the older broad category hook. This is a test proposal, not a predicted lift.

- Record one exact SKU, price, page, audience, disclosure and fulfillment terms before comparing messages.
- Compare A (previous category/feature hook) and B (specific use + demonstrated mechanism). Keep other elements as similar as possible; change one factor.
- Use existing organic channels and existing licensed assets. The experiment itself authorizes no advertising spend.
- Record views, outbound product clicks, checkout activity when actually instrumented, paid orders, net contribution, refunds, questions and traffic source. Never call outbound clicks checkout starts.
- If traffic cannot be randomized, call the result observational: posting time, platform distribution and audience can explain differences.
- Do not declare a statistical winner from a few clicks or invent an adequate sample threshold. Use a sample/power plan if traffic supports a controlled experiment; otherwise report raw counts and uncertainty.
- Until payment and fulfillment work, evaluate comprehension and qualified interest only; no inference of realized revenue.
- A/B publication remains subject to Ian's existing per-post approval. QA checks actual product truth and tracking; a QA pass does not establish market demand.

## Acceptance checklist

- Customer can identify what the item helps them do without understanding DTRT's AI project.
- Every objective claim has exact-SKU evidence, date, scope and any limitation.
- Relevant specifications and purchase terms remain easy to inspect.
- No 85/15 or 90/10 statement is presented as a scientific law.
- No health/medical, therapeutic or unmeasured productivity promise is introduced.
- Current stock, commerce and shipping status are described accurately.
- A demonstration is genuine/authorized; an illustration is labeled and not misrepresented as a test.
- No invented reviews, customer experiences, urgency, scarcity or revenue.
- Co-Founder approves positioning changes; Ian approves publication/spend under the current workflow.
- Report actual implementation separately from adoption, publication and sales results.
